\medskip\noindent\textbf{Supplementary Note 13. Replication across training seeds.}\par\smallskip
\begingroup\small\setlength{\parskip}{3pt}
\noindent\textit{Rule.} The sweep's readings and ranks at $b^*$ in the 13 ranked pairs are the prediction; the replication agrees with the sweep if each of the four large sweep gaps (0.04 or more within a pair) keeps its sign and the mean Kendall's $\tau_b$ over the 13 pairs is above zero by the sign-flip permutation test; everything else in this note is descriptive (Supplementary Notes 4 and 10). The reading is the sweep's: on the means over seeds 0--4, biology at $b^*$ by linear interpolation in batch score between the two refitted strengths, walking up from plain scVI at the new seeds and taking the first crossing. The test is one-sided over all $2^{13}$ sign patterns ($p<0.05$). It assumes that the 13 pairs' correlations are independent and symmetric about zero when the two orders are unrelated; this holds only roughly, because the two decoders of a task use the same task data and some tasks are related (two nested pairs), so its $p$-value is approximate. Two sensitivity analyses, which flip the signs per task and per task family, were added after the rule was fixed and are reported beside it, not as part of it (below). Because the rule tests only the sign of the within-pair differences of 0.04 or more and no precision calculation was made, the replication is not set up to separate penalties whose readings differ by less. Sweep (seeds 100--102) and replication (seeds 0--4) readings are reported separately.

\noindent\textit{Fits.} All 895 replication fits were scored and 0 failed: the 855 planned fits and 40 fits of the extension step, which refitted the next sweep strength once, with seeds 0--4, for the 8 readings whose new-seed means did not bracket $b^*$ (Supplementary Note 11). Plain scVI at seeds 0--4 reached batch scores within $-0.006$ to $0.005$ of the sweep's plain scVI in the 13 ranked pairs. Before the extension step 70 of the 78 readings bracketed $b^*$; after it 77 did. One reading, MMD on the pancreas task with the batch-conditioned decoder, did not replicate the crossing (its highest new-seed mean batch score was 0.674, against $b^*=0.684$) and takes the bottom place in its pair.

\noindent\textit{Readings.} Biology at $b^*$ on the new seeds differed from the sweep reading by a median of 0.004 and at most 0.024 (absolute differences over the 77 readings that reach $b^*$); the mean absolute difference per pair ranged from 0.002 to 0.011. In 7 readings the new-seed mean at the lower refitted strength had already reached $b^*$, so the reading interpolates from plain scVI at seeds 0--4. The first-ranked penalty was the same as in the sweep in 6 of 13 pairs; 29 of the 78 penalties kept their sweep rank and 56 moved by at most one place. Supplementary Table S9 gives every reading with the batch and biology scores of its two bracketing points.

\noindent\textit{Agreement.} Each of the four large sweep gaps kept its sign on the new seeds (4 of 4); the closest to flipping was the barycenter critic minus the reference critic on the small chromatin-accessibility task with the unconditioned decoder (sweep $+0.041$, replication $+0.013$). Kendall's $\tau_b$ ranged from $-0.067$ to $0.867$ over the 13 pairs (11 positive), with mean 0.456 and one-sided sign-flip $p=0.00049$ (4 of the $2^{13}$ sign patterns reach the observed mean). The agreement rule is met. Before the extension step that gap could not be read, because the barycenter critic's new-seed mean had not reached $b^*$; the other 3 gaps kept their sign and the mean $\tau_b$ was 0.426 ($p=0.00049$), so the rule was met only once the step it prescribes had been run.

\noindent\textit{Sensitivity analyses.} Sensitivity analysis, not part of the rule: with the signs flipped per task, both decoders of a task together (all $2^{8}$ patterns over the eight tasks), $p=0.0039$. Only the observed pattern reaches the observed mean (1 of 256), because the summed $\tau_b$ is positive in all 8 tasks, so this is the smallest $p$ that eight tasks allow. It keeps the two decoders of a task together but still flips the two tasks of each nested pair separately, so it is approximate as well (Rule, above). With the signs flipped per task family (the two tasks of each nested pair and both decoders together; all $2^{6}$ patterns over six families), $p=0.0156$. Only the observed pattern reaches the observed mean (1 of 64), because the summed $\tau_b$ is positive in all 6 families, so this is the smallest $p$ that six families allow; it was defined after the rule and is approximate as well (Rule, above).

\noindent\textit{Near-ties and slope-adjusted reading.} Of the 160 sweep near-ties (differences under 0.02), 155 kept a replication difference within $\pm0.04$ (127 before the extension step). Near-tied penalties stayed close, but the rule tests only the sign of the large gaps, so their order is not tested by it (Rule, above). The slope-adjusted reading, a sensitivity analysis whose formula was defined after the rule was fixed (the rule names it without one), kept the sign of 4 of the 4 large gaps, with mean $\tau_b$ 0.374 and $p=0.00073$.

\noindent\textit{Mean ranks on the new seeds.} Mean ranks over the ranked real tasks on the new seeds, recomputed from the replication ranks of Supplementary Table~S9 (sweep mean ranks in brackets), were, with the batch-conditioned decoder (5 tasks), the discriminator 5.20 (5.00), the reference critic 2.60 (3.80), the pooled critic 3.60 (2.20), the barycenter critic 3.60 (3.00), MMD 3.80 (4.60), the Sinkhorn divergence 2.20 (2.40); with the unconditioned decoder (6 tasks), the discriminator 3.00 (3.50), the reference critic 3.83 (3.33), the pooled critic 2.67 (3.33), the barycenter critic 4.17 (4.00), MMD 3.17 (2.17), the Sinkhorn divergence 4.17 (4.67). The penalty with the best mean rank changed with both decoders: the Sinkhorn divergence replaced the pooled critic with the batch-conditioned decoder, and the pooled critic replaced MMD with the unconditioned decoder. These mean ranks are descriptive, are not part of the agreement rule and were computed after the replication had been read (\texttt{paper/tools/replication\_mean\_ranks.py}).
